the present porphyrins 1 are suitable host to quinone guest in view of the binding constant and the binding mode.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the porphyrins having two or more convergent hydroxynaphthly1 groups can form multipoint complexes with ubiquinone derivatives via hydrogen bonding.
the porphyrin skeleton can be used as a hydrogen bonding receptor to recognize the structure of quinones.
porphyrin can recognize quinone derivatives with various substituents via multipoint hydrogen bonding fixation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding mode of porphyrin with quinone is largely dependent on the molecular structure of porphyrins.
the porphyrins having four hydroxynaphthly groups at meso positions can interact with various quinones through multipoint hydrogen bonding fixation.
multipoint hydrogen bonding fixation of porphyrins with quinones is a powerful tool for the design of molecular recognition.
